Norovirus Outbreak Hits Poland’s Hospitality Sector, Hundreds of Sites Disrupted

A norovirus outbreak has struck the Polish hospitality industry, resulting in widespread staff shortages and temporary closures across hundreds of hotels and restaurants nationwide. The outbreak, which began last week in the city of Wrocław, has since been reported at sites in Warsaw, Kraków, and Gdańsk, according to the Polish Association of Hospitality Operators.

Industry officials say the highly contagious gastrointestinal virus has affected more than 2,000 hospitality workers so far, leading to a wave of absenteeism and forcing management to shutter or reduce operations at affected sites. In some cases, entire hotel floors and restaurant dining rooms have been closed for deep cleaning, while other venues have switched to limited menus and reduced service hours.

“We are facing an unprecedented challenge,” said Tomasz Nowicki, spokesperson for the association. “Many sites are operating with skeletal staff, and several have had to close their doors temporarily to contain the outbreak and protect both employees and guests.”

The impact is being felt by both large hotel chains and independent establishments. Warsaw-based hotel group Złota Hospitality reported that 15% of its workforce is currently on sick leave. “We are working closely with health authorities to implement rigorous sanitation protocols,” said Marzena Kwiatkowska, the company’s operations director. “Our priority is the safety of our staff and guests.”

Unions representing hospitality workers have raised concerns about working conditions amid the outbreak. “Staff are under enormous pressure, and many are worried about job security if sites remain closed for an extended period,” said Piotr Zieliński, leader of the Hospitality Employees’ Union.

Analysts warn that the ongoing outbreak poses a significant threat to revenue during the busy summer season. “The hospitality industry relies heavily on in-person service, which makes it particularly vulnerable to contagious diseases,” said Agnieszka Słomka, analyst at Insight Hospitality Research. “Recovery will depend on how quickly the outbreak can be contained.”

Health authorities continue to monitor the situation as disinfection procedures and staff screenings remain in effect.
